title: Authentication Security Enforcement & MFA Policy Validation

observations.finding: MFA is enforced in authenticate middleware for platform admins and optionally configured role keys; bootstrap endpoints are exempt.
MFA_REQUIRED_ROLE_KEYS is deployment-configurable; default configuration behavior requires operational policy review.
Required users without verified TOTP receive MFA_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED; required users without a fresh challenge receive MFA_CHALLENGE_REQUIRED.
MFA freshness window is 300 seconds (5 minutes).
TOTP enrollment is two-step; pending factors are not marked verified until successful challenge.
TOTP uses six digits, SHA1, and a 30-second period; pending enrollment expires after 600 seconds.
TOTP secrets are encrypted at rest via configured MFA encryption key; configuration and rotation readiness require deployment review.
Recovery codes are generated on first factor verification; code hashes are stored and use is claimed once.
Challenge and enrollment rate limits are defined for IP and user scopes.
MFA failures emit abuse-event and audit-log evidence in source.
MFA factor disable requires a valid TOTP code, consumes a time step, deletes recovery codes, and clears active-session MFA freshness.
No live MFA-required role policy, database, runtime, concurrency, client UX, or security acceptance tests were executed in this phase.

policyMatrix.required: If role key is included in MFA_REQUIRED_ROLE_KEYS

policyMatrix.policySource: No platform-admin flag or configured role match

limitations: Enrollment/challenge/recovery behavior not tested against live database
Web/mobile flows and E2E not tested
